summary: Message sends, claims, and intent declarations from peer-bound harnesses must name their own agent as sender; attempts to impersonate another agent, a person, or the daemon are refused before message acceptance or publication.

replay.detail: Existing messages and replay remain unchanged.

compatibility.detail: POST /v1/messages, message.sent claims through POST /v1/claims, and message declarations through POST /v1/intent/apply return foreign-agent-actor when a peer-bound caller names a different normalized sender. Bound message.sent claims require a non-null sender, and bound message declarations require an explicit sender, checked before writes or idempotency replay. Its own agent label, short name, and stable identity are accepted for message sends and declarations. Unbound trusted-local callers retain sender selection, including declaration defaults; authenticated client send paths keep their existing authorization.

downtime.detail: No migration or fleet coordination required; normal daemon deployment activates the check.

manual.detail: Normal harness sends already use their own identity. A bound harness can no longer use the local CLI's explicit non-agent sender override.

recovery.detail: Revert the commit; stored messages require no conversion.
